item.title: 💗 Career tip: Make your CV easier to scan. Your experience might be relevant, bu
item.description:
💗 Career tip: Make your CV easier to scan.

Your experience might be relevant, but can a recruiter find it quickly?

A few things worth checking:

• Clear job titles - Make your previous roles easy to understand.
• Relevant experience - Highlight the work that matches the position.
• Specific achievements - Show what you accomplished, not just what you were responsible for.
• Simple formatting - Keep sections organized and easy to read.

Try this: Open your CV and scan it for 15 seconds.

Can you quickly identify your most relevant experience and strongest qualifications?

If not, it might be time to simplify a few things.

item.title: 💗 What does “equivalent experience” mean in a job description? You might see a r
item.description:
💗 What does “equivalent experience” mean in a job description?

You might see a requirement like:
“Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, or equivalent experience.”

This means the employer may consider relevant professional experience instead of a formal degree.

That experience could come from previous jobs, freelance work or projects where you've developed the skills needed for the role.

It doesn't mean every type of experience will qualify, but it does mean a degree isn't necessarily the only way to meet the requirement.

If you see “or equivalent experience,” focus on demonstrating how your actual work matches what the company is looking for.

item.description:
💗 Your next Web3 job might not have the title you're searching for.

Job titles aren't always consistent across companies and relying on one exact title could mean missing relevant opportunities.

🔜 Here's how to broaden your search:

• Search by responsibilities: Focus on the work you want to do, not just the position name.

• Explore related categories: Different titles can involve overlapping skills and responsibilities.

• Use filters: Narrow results by location, experience level, employment type and other requirements.

• Read the full description: The responsibilities often tell you more than the job title.

The takeaway: Don't limit your next opportunity to the title on your current CV.

item.title: 💗 A job offer mentions a “probation period.” What does that mean? A probation pe
item.description:
💗 A job offer mentions a “probation period.”
What does that mean?

A probation period is an initial stage of employment during which a company evaluates a new employee's performance, suitability for the role and how they're adapting to the team.

Depending on local employment laws and the contract, this period may involve specific performance reviews or different notice requirements.

But being on probation doesn't automatically mean an employee has no employment rights.

Before accepting a position, it's worth checking how long the probation period lasts, how performance will be evaluated and whether any employment conditions change during that time.

The rules vary by country, so understanding the terms of the agreement is important.

item.title: 💗 Do you need a portfolio if you're not a developer or designer? Not necessarily
item.description:
💗 Do you need a portfolio if you're not a developer or designer?

Not necessarily, but having examples of your work can help you stand out when applying for Web3 jobs.

And a portfolio doesn't have to be a fancy website!

Whether you work in marketing, community management, customer support, BD or operations, you can use a simple Notion page, Google Doc or PDF to showcase your experience.

What should you include?

• Projects or campaigns you've worked on
• Problems you've helped solve
• Your specific responsibilities and contributions
• Results, improvements or lessons learned

For each example, explain what the challenge was, what you did and what happened as a result.

You don't need impressive numbers or dozens of projects. A few clear examples can help hiring teams understand your experience better than a list of responsibilities alone.

Just make sure you're not sharing confidential information or private company data.
